answer: Latency-skew identity throttling. Each agent identity gets a vertex in a request-timing graph, and admission requires its inter-arrival delta profile to match a slow human-paced sonnet cadence distribution. Synthetic bursts that violate the fit are queued and deprioritized. An attacker must sustain plausible timing jitter across every identity for days, paying real compute and wall-clock delay per sybil—cost scales with identity count, not just registration.
